primary.name: Avoidant Personality Disorder or Social Anxiety Disorder

filing.block_desc: Disorders of adult personality and behavior (F60-F69)

encounters.cc: brought to the clinic by her mother because of noticeable changes in her personality and daily functioning over the past year

lines: Brought to the clinic by her mother because of noticeable changes in her personality and daily functioning over the past year
According to her mother, the patient has gradually become more hesitant to engage in activities that involve interacting with others and has spent increasing amounts of time at home.
The patient was once described as a hardworking and motivated student who consistently excelled academically and socially.
She was offered a prestigious promotion at work several months ago—a position that she had frequently spoken about with excitement and that seemed aligned with her long-term career goals.
However, at the last moment, she declined the offer, stating that she was certain she would have performed poorly and humiliated herself in front of colleagues.
When asked further, she explains that even minor criticisms feel unbearable to her.
For example, she recalls leaving her previous job after a coworker made a mild remark about her presentation skills, an incident that she describes as “proof” that she is incapable and inadequate.
Since then, she has become increasingly reluctant to take on professional opportunities that could place her in a position of judgment.
Socially, she struggles to attend parties or group gatherings unless her sister accompanies her for reassurance.
At these events, she feels highly self-conscious and convinced that others are scrutinizing or mocking her, even when reassured otherwise.
Despite these difficulties, the patient emphasizes that she very much wants friendships and hopes to one day establish a successful career.
She spends significant time ruminating about how she is perceived and describes frequent worry that she will be rejected or embarrassed if she lets her guard down.
The patient herself states, “I wish I could just relax and join in like everyone else, but I always feel like people are judging me.
I can’t shake the fear that I’ll say something foolish or get laughed at.”
The mother reports no history of substance use or medical illness.
No known drug allergies (NKDA)
- Mother: Generalized anxiety disorder
- Father: Social anxiety disorder
- Paternal aunt: Major depressive disorder
Smoking: Never smoker.
Alcohol: No alcohol use.
Occupation: Junior Client Relations Associate.
She expresses sadness about her current situation but denies persistent depressed mood, hopelessness, or anhedonia.
She also denies hallucinations, delusions, history of trauma, or episodes of mania.
Her sleep and appetite are stable.
Her physical examination is unremarkable, with normal affect and intact cognition.
There are no neurological or systemic abnormalities.

encounters.cc: feeling extremely anxious in social situations

lines: Feeling extremely anxious in social situations

The patient returns for follow-up psychiatric evaluation, having initially presented in January 2020 when she was brought to the clinic by her mother due to progressive changes in personality and daily functioning.
She reports that this has been a problem since her teenage years but has worsened since she started a new job where she has to interact with many colleagues and clients.
She avoids company meetings and social gatherings, stating that she fears she will say something embarrassing and be laughed at.
She has a few close friends but often declines invitations to go out because she is worried about being judged by others.
